About us · Governance

Leadership and governance

The Directorate General provides the institutional direction and development of ABS. Academic, administrative and teaching responsibilities are exercised in accordance with the internal organisation and the procedures in force.

Legal framework

A limited liability company governed by OHADA law

ABS — African Business School SARL is a limited liability company (SARL), whose registered office is in Bamako, Mali. The Statutory Manager performs her duties in accordance with the company's articles of association, the OHADA Uniform Act on commercial companies and economic interest groups (AUSCGIE), the provisions applicable in Mali and the decisions duly adopted by the partners.

In accordance with Article 323 and subsequent articles of the AUSCGIE, the SARL is administered by one or more managers, natural persons, appointed in the articles of association or by a subsequent instrument. The Statutory Manager provides the legal representation of the company and exercises the management and representation powers provided for by the applicable texts; the powers expressly reserved for the partners by law or by the articles of association remain within their remit.

Position identification

Legal designationStatutory Manager

Purpose of the role

The Statutory Manager, guarantor of institutional coherence

The Statutory Manager provides the general management, legal representation, strategic steering and operational management of ABS — African Business School SARL. She guarantees the coherence between the institution's vision, its regulatory obligations, its resources, its development ambitions and its results. She drives this ambition within the framework of the ABS 2035 Strategic Plan, which aims to position ABS as an institution recognised for academic and professional excellence, the quality and relevance of its programmes, pedagogical and technological innovation and the professional readiness of its graduates.

Leadership and institutional strategy

  • Define the vision and strategic directions of ABS
  • Design and drive the ABS 2035 Strategic Plan
  • Position ABS as a leading pan-African institution
  • Ensure coherence between strategic ambitions and available resources

Legal representation and governance

  • Provide the executive direction of the company and represent it legally before third parties
  • Sign contracts and agreements falling within her powers, in accordance with the AUSCGIE and the articles of association
  • Ensure the regularity of legal, administrative and institutional formalities

Academic development and quality

  • Define the general directions of academic development, in coordination with the Rectorate
  • Oversee the evolution of the programme offering and support the continuous improvement of teaching quality
  • Encourage academic and scientific partnerships

Financial and economic management

  • Oversee the preparation of the annual budget and monitor the cash position
  • Review financial statements and accounting reports
  • Ensure control of expenses and the separation of authorisation, payment, recording and control functions

Partnerships, entrepreneurship and innovation

  • Develop strategic partnerships and relations with companies
  • Support the Career & Corporate Relations Center and grow ABS Startup Lab
  • Develop relations with pan-African and international networks

Digital transformation and sustainable development

  • Oversee digital transformation and the digitalisation of administrative processes
  • Promote the responsible use of artificial intelligence
  • Develop projects related to the green university and support initiatives contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals

Organisation

The governance chain

Hierarchical and functional reporting lines are set out in ABS's approved organisation chart. The functions presented below are based on the official job and position descriptions; only the functions are displayed, and the names, biographies and photographs of the officeholders are published with their consent.

  1. Director General

    Statutory Manager — Managing Director & CEO

    First executive authority of the company. She provides general management, legal representation, strategic steering and operational management, and supervises all directorates, departments and services.

    Top of the chain: appointed under the articles of association and the decisions of the partners

  2. Rector

    First academic authority

    He guarantees the quality, relevance and academic performance of the institution, defines the main academic directions in line with the ABS 2035 Strategic Plan and supervises the Director of Studies as well as the heads of fields.

    Hierarchical reporting line: Director General

  3. Director of Studies

    Academic organisation

    Operational manager for the organisation, coordination and monitoring of teaching activities. He implements the academic directions defined by the Rector and serves as the operational link with heads of fields, teachers, the registrar's office and students.

    Hierarchical reporting line: Rector · Institutional reporting line: Directorate General

  4. Registrar

    Academic administration and enrolment

    Responsible for academic administration and the centralised management of enrolment. Guarantor of the administrative traceability of each student's journey, from application and admission to graduation.

    Hierarchical reporting line: Directorate General · Functional reporting line: Rectorate

  5. Marketing and Communication Manager

    Image, visibility and recruitment

    Designs and implements the institution's marketing and communication strategy, develops its visibility and leads student recruitment campaigns.

    Hierarchical reporting line: Directorate General

  6. Accounting, cashier and administrative services

    Administrative and financial management

    The Accountant ensures reliable and compliant bookkeeping under the reporting framework applicable in Mali (revised SYSCOHADA); the Cashier guarantees secure and traceable handling of authorised receipts and disbursements.

    Hierarchical reporting line: Directorate General
